title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Iran is now hitting ship engine rooms near Hormuz, with at least 23 attacks in the first two weeks of October, and its foreign minister says the strait stays shut until the US meets Tehran's terms. Saudi air links are slowly coming back after Riyadh reopened, but flydubai and Etihad stay out to 24 October and Middle East airfreight rates are running 52% above last year.

stories.headline: Iran steps up Hormuz attacks and now aims at ship engine rooms
body: At least 23 ship attacks were logged in or near the Strait of Hormuz in the first two weeks of October, and at least five hit engine rooms, Bloomberg reports. None of those engine-room strikes happened in September. Two recently hit ships sank last week, including the container ship GFS Pride, and containers were reported adrift near the UAE.

On Tuesday Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed two more tankers were set ablaze by mines south of the strait. The shipping security centre JMIC said earlier claims had "no substantiation". Hormuz traffic was about 70% below prewar levels, with 254 transits in the week to 14 October.
stories.soWhat: New this week: Iran is going for ships that cannot be repaired at sea. Expect insurers and carriers to stay away from Gulf calls, so keep war-risk surcharges and east-coast routings in place.

stories.headline: Iran says Hormuz stays closed until the US accepts its terms
body: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Wednesday the strait will stay closed until Washington honours the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding. He said indirect talks continue through Pakistan and Qatar, and pointed to an Iranian "Seven-Day Plan" that would fully reopen the strait on day six.
Brent eased to $107.87 a barrel on Tuesday, down 1.8% in 24 hours.
stories.soWhat: There is a path to reopening on the table, but no date. Plan Q4 pricing and capacity on a closed strait, and keep a ready playbook for a fast reopening.

stories.headline: Riyadh reopens, but almost half of Saudi flights were lost in 12 days
body: Cirium data show 5,547 of 12,195 scheduled Saudi departures were cancelled or listed as no-fly from 8 to 19 October, about 45%. Riyadh's King Khalid airport, closed after Houthi attacks, reopened on Sunday.

What is new: Emirates is bringing back Riyadh and Jeddah flights on 20 and 21 October. Etihad and flydubai stay out of their Saudi points until 24 October. Air Arabia has cancelled Sharjah flights to Riyadh, Dammam and other cities with no restart date.
stories.soWhat: Belly space into KSA comes back first on Emirates from Dubai. Shift urgent Riyadh air from Abu Dhabi and Sharjah to Dubai departures, and keep road as the default.

stories.headline: Airlines lift surcharges as Middle East air rates run 52% above last year
body: WorldACD says Middle East and South Asia air rates in September were flat on August but up 52% year on year, the steepest rise of any region. Global rates were 25% higher.
Carriers are passing on costs. MSC Air Cargo raised its surcharge from $1.70 to $2.30 per kg from 16 October. Air Canada Cargo raises surcharges from 26 October, citing "Middle East unrest" and fuel.
stories.soWhat: Airline costs are rising into peak season. Our air express and freight rates need to pass on carrier surcharges as they land, not at year-end.

stories.headline: UAE warehouse tenants stay put as demand moves north and east
body: Warehouse lease renewals rose 21.6% to a record of about 8,200 in the first half, while new contracts fell 51.8%. Rents rose another 12.4%, says Cavendish Maxwell.

Rerouted cargo is pulling demand to the Northern Emirates and the east coast. More than 10 million sq ft of space opened there in the first half, including 5.2 million in Umm Al Quwain, where rents fell 18.5%.
stories.soWhat: Dubai space is tight and costly, but the north is cheap and near Khor Fakkan. Price contract logistics with a Northern Emirates option for clients who need room.

competitors.name: Emirates SkyCargo
competitors.headline: Emirates is growing its freighter fleet fast
body: Emirates SkyCargo has taken seven Boeing 777 freighters since March and its first converted 777-300ERSF. It expects 23 dedicated freighters by the end of March 2027. Freighter destinations rose from just over 40 in March to more than 60 by July.
South American exports rose 18% to over 22,000 tonnes since April. Expeditors says SkyCargo serves 137 destinations, but Class 1 dangerous goods are still restricted.
competitors.soWhat: Emirates has the most freighter lift out of Dubai and owns Emirates Courier Express. Lock in block space with SkyCargo before peak, and watch for its courier arm using that capacity on price.

competitors.name: DHL
competitors.headline: DHL signs up Dubai manufacturers with preferential export rates
body: Dubai's Department of Economy and Tourism has teamed up with DHL under its Export Assistance Programme. Eligible members get preferential shipping rates, tailored logistics and end-to-end supply chain support. More than 50 manufacturers attended a DHL-led workshop.
DHL Global Forwarding UAE said "rising landed costs and longer lead times are putting pressure on their margins."
competitors.soWhat: DHL is using a government channel to lock in Dubai exporters. We should pitch our own export package to Dubai Industries and the D33 manufacturing programmes.

competitors.name: FedEx
competitors.headline: FedEx sets the 2027 price bar at 5.9%
body: FedEx raises standard rates by an average 5.9% from 4 January 2027, including import and export volume. The international additional handling surcharge for dimensions rises from $29.50 to $32.25. A $25 fee will apply when trade documents are sent on paper.
competitors.soWhat: Rate season has started. A 5.9% global benchmark gives us cover to set our own 2027 increase at a similar level, above it where war costs justify.

opportunities.title: Dubai departures for KSA air
opportunities.text: Emirates is back in Riyadh and Jeddah from 20–21 October while Etihad, flydubai and Air Arabia stay out. Route urgent KSA air via DXB.

opportunities.title: Northern Emirates storage
opportunities.text: Over 10m sq ft of new space and rents down 18.5% in Umm Al Quwain. Offer cheaper contract logistics near the east-coast ports.

opportunities.title: Exporters squeezed on margin
opportunities.text: Dubai manufacturers face rising landed costs and longer lead times. A bundled export offer with customs and road to KSA can win them.

opportunities.title: 2027 rate reset
opportunities.text: FedEx's 5.9% average increase sets a market benchmark. Use it to reset tariffs and lift under-priced contracts.

opportunities.title: Reopening playbook
opportunities.text: Iran has floated a plan to reopen Hormuz within a week. Shippers who are ready first will win the backlog.

watchouts.title: Engine-room strikes
watchouts.text: At least five engine-room hits in two weeks and a sunk container ship. Ship and cargo cover may tighten further.

watchouts.title: No reopening date
watchouts.text: Iran ties Hormuz to US concessions. Do not price for a quick return to Jebel Ali direct calls.

watchouts.title: Air costs into peak
watchouts.text: Regional air rates are up 52% and airlines keep adding surcharges. Margin on fixed-rate air contracts is at risk.

watchouts.title: KSA air still patchy
watchouts.text: Almost half of Saudi flights were lost in 12 days, and three UAE airlines stay out to at least 24 October.

watchouts.title: Dubai warehouse rents
watchouts.text: Rents are up another 12.4%. Contract logistics renewals must reflect our own higher costs.

moves.title: Move urgent KSA air to Dubai departures
moves.text: Book Riyadh and Jeddah shipments on Emirates from DXB while Etihad and flydubai stay out to 24 October. Tell key accounts the change.

moves.title: Pass on new airline surcharges now
moves.text: Check our air rate cards against MSC, Air Canada and other carrier surcharge rises this month. Update fuel and security recovery before peak.

moves.title: Hold war-risk surcharges
moves.text: Engine-room attacks and Iran's stance mean no early cut. Review weekly, not monthly.

moves.title: Draft the 2027 general rate increase
moves.text: Use FedEx's 5.9% as a reference. Model a higher figure for lanes hit by war costs.

moves.title: Pitch an export package to Dubai manufacturers
moves.text: Answer DHL's DET deal with an export bundle for Dubai Industries members: customs, road to KSA and air.

moves.title: Add a Northern Emirates warehouse option
moves.text: Quote contract logistics clients a lower-cost site near Khor Fakkan and Umm Al Quwain.
